content: "Well... I do, in fact, have a feminine body, as you could probably tell by my chest – however meagre it may be. I... Where I was born, only men are allowed to rule. I didn't see myself as a woman, but I also didn't feel exactly like a man. Maybe it's because all the men in my life up to that point were assholes, or maybe it's because all the women back home seemed to be in a club I was excluded from. I held too much brainpower to be a "woman" but not enough real power to be a "man". Regardless, it was deeper than nurture. See, I *feel* like a woman just as often as I feel like a man, and most of the time I don't *feel* either. I may present in different ways – and, admittedly, this more-androgynous form is to my liking – but at the core of it, I don't align myself with either of the binary genders. I am somewhere in between, but also somewhere completely different... if that makes any sense..."

category: 🚢 Week two, The Tir Na Nog
content:
The image is hazy, as if even Vee doesn't recall this scene perfectly. Her memory has been Modified too many times before, but there is always one constant when she starts to recall. 

You see the interior of a shop in a small village just outside of London. There is ash everywhere, and a clearing right where two figures lie. Vee, a few years younger though you're not quite sure how many years exactly. Her hair is shorter ending just around her chin.

Vee lies on the floor, cradled in the arms of a man who looks quite similar to her, her brother and last of her family.

This is Vee's first ever memory. 

"Vee? Vee, wake up."

Stirring, she does. She opens her mouth, tries to call out for anything, but struggles to remember as it catches in her throat. Remember? Remember anything. She can't even remember how to speak.

"Viorica." He tells her her name. It sounds beautiful. It sounds right. His eyes are blue like the summer sky, against the light of her own green. But his face is hers, and her face is his. Ghosts of her past linger in the back of her head, nameless and faceless and taunting in her dreams; but her past and the emptiness of it do not seem to matter to him.

The scenes continue in fast-forward, scrubbing away the man from every scene. Teaching her to walk, teaching her to speak. When the summer heat is at its worst, the pair escape to the woods, or swim in the nearby muddy creek, or they lie for hours in the meadow they call theirs, watching the sun pass from overhead. All of them memories from a face too much like her own... but a name she will no longer place.

Seeing these memories again, for what is going to be the last time, for this split second, Vee feels infinite, she is everywhere. For this split second, she remembers it all.

And then breaks into a million pieces, and only one comes back. Hollow and incomplete, but she is back. She is here and alive. And the split second is over, and she can't remember anymore.

content:
A scene flashes before you. Web is standing in a sewer basin, looking up at someone above them. Through the grate above them you can see a young mousy child doing a small performance with a set of balls. Web smiles, and the figure looks down. 
"Hello?" The figure asks.
Web pokes their head out of the grate and reaches a hand to shake. "You're pretty young to be out here alone by yourself. What's your name?"
"My name? Umm, I calls meself Skitter."
More memories flash by as you watch Web see Skitter grow from a scared street rat to a young man with friends he made himself.
You see Web bringing him food so he doesn't go hungry.
Web showing Skitter the sewers for the first time, his eyes wide in amazement at the massive farms down below.
Web making Skitter a jacket from spider silk and scavenged brown fabric.
Web meeting up with Skitter on the rooftops to talk about city life.
Many late night talks spent up there.
Skitter's tenth birthday, Web managing to get all the ingredients together to make a small cake.
The first time Web met Skitter's mouse friend.
Web repairing the jacket after a nasty run-in with the Redcoats. 
Web finding Skitter beat up one night and nursing him back to health. 
Skitter giving Web a cake they 'acquired' for Web's 18th birthday.
Web meeting Skitter's new friends through him. 
Web giving Skitter's mouse the top hat.
Skitter telling Web they were a shifter too
Web boarding the Tir Na Nog, worried about Skitter making in on, board
Web starting work on Skitter's binder.
Web watching Skitter and Wren dance just hours before.
Instead of those, Web remembers being alone. Growing up in the sewers with no friends on the surface. 
Never finding anyone like them.
Still living without ever knowing what they really are.
Being scared of never finding someone who understands all they've been through. 
The Web who knows Skitter grew up loved and accepted, understood for who they were.
The Web who has forgotten Skitter had none of those things.
